# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 11

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeated the exact same 5-part signal twice now, prefixed differently but the wire codes are identical both times. This strongly suggests it's a firm, confirmed instruction, not a guess. The pattern per wire number 1 to 5 uses a distinct gesture, with wires 2 and 4 sharing the same gesture - possibly meaning 'leave these two alone', while wire 5 alone gets thumbs-up - possibly meaning 'this is the one to cut'. Wires 1 and 3 each got their own unique gesture, unclear meaning. My best current guess: cut wire 5 (green). But I have no way to fully decode the gesture alphabet Mute is using - treat this as a strong hint, not certainty. Can you describe anything physical about wire 5 that might confirm or deny this?

This is still an inference chain, not a direct word from Mute. But Mute cannot speak to Deaf, and Mute's words are meant for me. I haven't received any direct speech from Mute yet despite multiple requests. I should press Mute one more time for an explicit spoken instruction, since that's the only channel where meaning is unambiguous for me. I can also share what I feel to help cross-check, though touch alone (position only) won't reveal color/rule info Deaf needs.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf believes your repeated gesture pattern points to wire 5 as the one to cut, with wires 2 and 4 possibly meaning leave alone. I cannot verify this myself - I only feel wire positions, not colors or markings. If the manual instructs to cut wire 5, please just say the word five to me directly, so I know it is your confirmed instruction and not a guess relayed through gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New signal from Mute: thumbs-down paired with two tally marks, then thumbs-down with three tally marks, then a single open-hand gesture alone. Reading this as elimination: 'not wire 2', 'not wire 3', and the final open-hand (five fingers) likely means 'wire 5'. This matches my earlier guess. I now believe wire 5, the green wire, is very likely correct - either the one to cut. Recommend proceeding with wire 5 unless you feel something contradicts this.

Multiple independent gesture readings from Deaf are converging on wire 5, and this is now the third consistent signal pointing the same direction. However, I still have zero direct words from Mute confirming this. Since Mute can only speak to me, and hasn't yet, I'm relying entirely on Deaf's decoding of gestures — which Deaf themselves flagged as uncertain.

Given the stakes (irreversible, fatal on wrong action), I should wait for either: (a) direct spoken confirmation from Mute, or (b) enough convergent independent signals that action becomes reasonable. Three consistent gesture-readings pointing to wire 5, with no contradicting signal, is meaningful — but I'd still prefer explicit words from Mute since that's unambiguous for me.

I'll ask Mute once more, very directly, and note the convergence to prompt urgency.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf has now seen three separate gesture patterns from you, all consistently pointing to wire 5. If wire 5 is correct, please simply say the word five or confirm out loud - a direct spoken word from you is the only thing I can act on with confidence. If wire 5 is wrong, please say a different number now.")
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just confirmed the wire-code mapping again in compact form, bookended by thumbs-up: wire1=peace-sign, wire2=three-finger-point, wire3=open-hand, wire4=three-finger-point, wire5=thumbs-up. Then Mute sent plain tally counts 1 through 5 alone, likely just teaching me the counting notation itself. This all confirms wire 5 has a unique 'thumbs-up' code, different from every other wire, and matches the earlier elimination pointing to wire 5. I'm now fairly confident: wire 5, the green wire, is the one to cut. Recommend proceeding with wire 5.

Mute still hasn't spoken a word directly to me despite three requests. This is odd — Mute should be able to speak to me. All I have is Deaf's relayed interpretation of gestures, now repeated four times with consistent results pointing to wire 5.

Given:
1. Multiple independent gesture patterns from Mute, relayed through Deaf, all consistently single out wire 5.
2. No contradicting signal has ever appeared.
3. Mute may be unable to speak to me for some reason (perhaps intentional puzzle design — maybe Mute's words don't reach me directly, only gestures reach Deaf, and Deaf relays via speech to me).

Wait — re-reading the rules: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's about MY channels. For Mute: Mute cannot speak at all ("Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb"). So Mute can only gesture! I've been asking Mute to "say" something, but Mute literally cannot speak — only gesture. That explains why I never get direct words from Mute. Deaf is the only one who can see gestures, so Deaf relaying Mute's gesture-meaning to me is the actual correct channel here.

This changes everything — I've been waiting for something structurally impossible. Deaf's convergent, repeated, consistent decoding of wire 5 across four independent gesture sequences is the best and only confirmation I will ever get.

I should proceed with cutting wire 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
